cards.title: What the settings mean
cards.content:
**Required**

- **Enable energy sales** — allows this policy to prepare a candidate; EMS still controls execution.
- **Maximum export power** — limits power discharged from battery storage to the grid.
- **Automatic home-energy protection** — retains the energy needed for forecast home consumption.

**Optional**

- **Additional protection from sale** — adds 0–90 percentage points to the battery reserve while automatic home-energy protection is enabled. Applies to RCE and Pstryk. The total is capped at 100%; the home can still use this extra reserve.
- **Export lockout hours** — exclude the selected hours from the RCE plan.

The value shown in every field is the effective value. If the
readiness card reports missing data, the plan remains informational and does not
receive execution authority.

cards.title: Plan execution eligibility
How energy sales automation works
cards.content:
The automation requires the external integration
**Solcast PV Forecast** by **BJReplay**:
[installation and configuration](https://github.com/BJReplay/ha-solcast-solar).

Forecasts for **today** and **tomorrow** are required.
If Solcast provides a **day-three forecast**, the integration uses it
automatically to value energy worth retaining after the end of the
48-hour market horizon. Its absence does not block operation. Entities are
detected automatically in Polish and English HA; for
custom names, the Today and Tomorrow entities can be entered above.

The optimizer simulates the balance every 30 minutes from now through tonight,
the whole next day and the following night until **90 minutes after sunrise**.
It first withholds the emergency Self-Use reserve and the safety
correction, and the full forecast home consumption through
the end of the nearest protected night from export. Forecast PV before sunset does not
reduce this night reserve. Only the remaining energy is assigned
to the most valuable available RCE slots today or tomorrow.

The export price is not configured manually. The optimizer compares
the full financial result of every available slot in the horizon,
selects the highest prices and includes natural PV export, battery-storage
wear, and the value of energy retained for the next day.
An earlier discharge is used only when it increases the net result
or creates battery-storage headroom before a later surplus sold
more cheaply.

System power is calculated as **one inverter's rated power × the automatically
detected inverter count × the configured discharge percentage**.
Until at least 24 hours of history has been collected, the fallback
daily consumption entered above is used. The algorithm then learns from up to
28 complete days, gives recent days more weight, rejects
isolated spikes, and builds separate 48 half-hour profiles
for weekdays and weekends. The latest four days remain a fast
fallback after a fresh installation. Actual coverage and the selected
model are shown in diagnostics.

The reserve is conservatively derived from Solcast **P10/P50/P90**
bands and forecast error measured on previous days. During
the day, correction compares forecast with actual production but does not
reduce home protection based on a short post-sunrise sample.

The Self-Use reserve setting is not changed. That energy remains available
below the normal threshold only during a grid outage.

cards.title: Estimated low-cost charging energy — last 30 days
How tariff charging works
cards.content:
The automation forecasts home consumption and PV production, then checks
whether energy will last until the next low-cost period. If not,
it selects the cheapest available slots and charges only as much as
is actually needed. It protects the configured SOC reserve and accounts for losses.
The planners may be enabled at the same time; EMS selects only one safe
execution action.

cards.title: How tariff automation works — details
cards.content:
The automation uses the same **Solcast PV Forecast** and
actual home-load history as RCE. Every 30 minutes it simulates
the balance through the end of tomorrow and, once a day-three forecast is detected automatically,
the following day as well. In **grid-charging** mode, the configured power is a shared AC-input
limit: the inverter first supplies current home loads and only then uses
the remaining power to charge
the battery to its target SOC. If the goal is only to preserve
energy in battery storage for later peak-price hours, the automation freezes
SOC and uses the grid for the home load — it does not try to charge
battery storage above that level.

The physical planning reserve always equals the current
**Self-Use reserve**. The separate demand margin is
a percentage of the base energy deficit in the next protected period:
it may be consumed by the home and does not raise the Self-Use floor. First
the base deficit is covered, followed by the margin; power, time and
maximum-SOC constraints are exposed as the infeasible portion.

After collecting a reliable amount of daytime production, the automation compares
actual energy with the Solcast curve. Sustained underproduction, such as a disabled
PV string, lowers only today's forecast and lets the plan be corrected
before the next low-price window. Small samples just after sunrise are
ignored.

In winter, with low production and high consumption, it may retain energy in battery storage
the battery during the low-price period and additionally charge it for
the following expensive hours. Total system power, maximum SOC and
separate BMS charge/discharge limits and conversion losses are included in
the calculation. A marginal energy shift is rejected when
the price spread does not cover losses and the automatically assumed
battery wear cost.

The load model uses up to 28 complete days, gives greater weight to
recent observations, and separates weekday and
weekend profiles. The plan uses P10/P50/P90 uncertainty bands, retains
a terminal reserve, and does not react to every small forecast
change. During actual grid charging it also measures delivered power;
after several reliable samples it corrects future lead times,
without learning from ramp-up or charge taper near 100% SOC.

RCE, tariff charging and RCEm can be enabled at the same time.
EMS selects one safe execution action; manual EMS schedules
retain priority.

The **PGE, TAURON, ENEA, ENERGA and STOEN** profiles automatically select
time periods, weekends, Polish public holidays and — where required —
the summer or winter season. Indicative prices use the 2026 tariffs
of the regional incumbent supplier and selected DSO.

A user with another supplier selects the **Manual** profile and enters the total
variable price per kWh from their bill: energy, variable distribution,
quality, RES and cogeneration charges. Fixed charges are excluded
because they do not depend on the charging time.

[URE offer comparison](https://maszwybor.ure.gov.pl/or/cenki/122,Cenowy-Energetyczny-Kalkulator-Internetowy-CENKI.html)
· [DSO tariffs and time periods](https://www.ure.gov.pl/pl/energia-elektryczna/ceny-wskazniki/7852,Taryfy-opublikowane-w-2026-r.html)

cards.title: What the settings mean
cards.content:
**Required**

- **Enable voltage management** — allows RCEm to prepare its own candidate.
- **Maximum export permitted by the grid agreement** — is a hard limit that RCEm cannot exceed.

**Optional**

- **Smooth export control** — reduces export as voltage rises.
- **Create battery headroom** — may schedule an earlier partial battery discharge.
- **Additional SOC reserve** — increases the reserve protected by RCEm only.

The values shown in the fields are effective values. A missing current
plan or lack of readiness blocks RCEm actions but does not block the Supervisor's other
polityk EMS.

cards.title: How RCEm responds to voltage
cards.content:
During normal regulation, the automation remains in
**Self-Use**. It combines the Solcast forecast for today and tomorrow,
the actual four-day home-load profile, SOC, battery capacity,
and historical L1/L2/L3 voltages. The highest phase always has
priority. As voltage rises, RCEm selects a safe
charging or export limit according to the current plan and readbacks.

cards.title: How it protects the battery-storage reserve
cards.content:
Home consumption is subtracted from the PV forecast; only the remaining
surplus requires battery headroom. RCEm accounts for headroom that
will arise naturally as the battery supplies the home before the peak. The
preparation cycle ends upon reaching the target SOC, or
earlier if the highest phase reaches 248.4 V or the
10-minute average reaches 249.2 V. It never discharges below the protected
home-and-outage-reserve SOC.

cards.title: How it accounts for zero export
cards.content:
Morning discharge requires EMS execution mode, RCEm permission,
active GCF, and a confirmed export limit above 0%
with no export lockout. When the limit is 0%, grid discharge
does not receive execution authority and the plan remains
informational only. RCEm does not enable GCF; the user enables it deliberately.

Optional export control changes only the maximum export limit
and never exceeds the lower of these values: the limit
found at startup and the **Maximum export permitted by the grid
agreement** field.

cards.title: How it creates battery headroom for PV
cards.content:
If capacity is still missing after accounting for home supply,
the **Create battery headroom before high PV production** option may
schedule discharge only for the calculated shortfall. Power is based on
the required energy and time until the period, with a 30-minute buffer.

Before the predicted peak, RCEm may limit the maximum battery
charging power to avoid filling it too early. The calculated plan
does not confirm physical execution.

cards.title: How it works with EMS
cards.content:
The RCEm planner does not write to the inverter. EMS independently checks
readiness, grants one owner, issues the command, confirms physical
readback, and restores the pre-transaction settings afterward.

RCE, tariff charging, and voltage management may be enabled at the same time. EMS
selects one safe action; battery balancing and manual EMS plans
retain their own priority gates.

cards.title: What happens when data is unavailable
cards.content:
A missing current plan, voltage history, forecast, or required
readback blocks only the RCEm action that needs that data.
It does not disable EMS or block the current safe tariff-charging or RCE
policy. Uncertain values are shown as **No data**, without granting
execution authority.

cards.title: Limitations and diagnostics
cards.content:
RCEm does not change three-phase imbalance, Q(U), P(U), power
factor, or protection thresholds. It is energy-management automation, not
certified grid protection.

The sole executor may change the charging limit by at most 10 percentage points
per minute and the export limit by 5–15 percentage points, depending on
voltage. At 253 V, export may be reduced immediately to
0%, and the battery uses the full safe BMS limit. Full profiles,
equations, historical periods, and controller values are available under
**Show full RCEm calculations** and in expert diagnostics.

detail_cards.title: How battery balancing works
detail_cards.content:
A periodic service cycle for LiFePO4 batteries. On the scheduled day it
first uses PV production and the normal BMS limit to 95% SOC.
From the first valid reading at or above 95%, it maintains slow
charging at approximately 0.4 kW net for the complete battery. After sunset it uses
verified grid charging and adds home consumption exactly once.
The configured balancing hold starts only after physical
acknowledgement of the mode and settings at 99.9% SOC.

During the cycle, RCE, tariff charging, and manual EMS schedules are
blocked by existing EMS ownership; their settings remain
unchanged. A short Self-Use freshness gap only pauses
writes, while safety failures stop the cycle immediately. Completion
or disabling the feature restores the exact prior settings and EMS mode;
physical Off-Grid operation always has priority. Use this feature in accordance
with the battery-storage manufacturer's recommendations.

cards.title: How to read energy-flow directions
cards.content:
The arrow indicates the direction of energy flow. PV flows are
metered values published by the inverter. Items marked as
diagnostic or estimated come from the energy balance and are not an exact
meter of physical direction. Exact grid → battery-storage flow is
shown only when the installation provides a fresh
physical measurement; without that source, the status remains “No data”.
